roleKicker: Full-stack Software Engineer // Engineering Lead // Technical Writer
aboutMe: I’m Divine Orji, a full-stack software engineer and Head of Engineering at The Kreativ Studio, where I lead a remote team and stay hands-on across frontend, backend, and deployment.
I also write technical guides on my blog and created the software engineering curriculum behind Alchemy Of Code to help learners turn ideas into working software.
speakerBio: Divine Orji is a full-stack software engineer, technical writer, and Head of Engineering at The Kreativ Studio, where he leads a remote team and builds web products such as Bonjour Quick Bites, Noma, Merphils, and Grooovy. He writes hands-on guides on his blog and created the software engineering curriculum behind Alchemy Of Code. His work focuses on building useful software and helping others learn to build their own.

selectedWork.title: Bonjour Quick Bites
selectedWork.summary: Port Harcourt customers use this storefront to order fresh bread, pastries, and hot meals for outlet pickup or doorstep delivery. I built it end to end with Next.js, TypeScript, Supabase, and Better Auth, backed by GitHub and Vercel for CI/CD.

selectedWork.title: Crunchies Online
selectedWork.summary: Over a seven-month redesign in Next.js and Tailwind CSS, I reworked checkout, pickup, and delivery location selection and wired up Google Maps outlet discovery. Monthly online sales grew from ₦200,000 to over ₦3 million.

selectedWork.title: Alchemy Of Code
selectedWork.summary: Behind this learning platform is a software engineering curriculum I wrote to help people move from fundamentals to shipping their own ideas. Under the hood, it runs on Cloudflare with Supabase and Better Auth.

selectedWork.title: Noma
selectedWork.summary: I built Noma for nursing students prepping for exams, pairing quick flashcards for revising key concepts with quizzes that show what’s actually sticking.

selectedWork.title: The Iroko Circle
selectedWork.summary: For this African literature community, my focus was designing and building a WordPress publishing home where readers can discover new stories, writers can submit work, and members can find local chapters.

highlights.quote: A thoughtful product engineer who helped grow monthly revenue from N200,000 to N3 million by turning 3 core ordering decisions - delivery, pickup, and location selection - into a smoother flow that made the platform easier for customers to use.
Divine explains technical topics in a grounded way that makes them easier to understand and apply.
An effective UI improvement partner who made our existing WordPress and Elementor website clearer and gave clients a better path to send enquiries.
A professional who consistently delivers high-quality technical documentation and exceptional front-end development work, with the reliability to meet tight deadlines.
An engineer whose deep technical knowledge shines in the content itself, with a way of explaining complex subjects that makes the material actually stick.
A dependable developer and writer who always meets deadlines with a high standard and close attention to detail.
A brilliant developer whose products are seamless and pixel-perfect, with writing that provides total clarity and a genuine passion for helping and mentoring new developers in the community.
A patient and understanding frontend developer who goes the extra mile, and a great leader who ensures everyone is carried along while constantly looking for opportunities to learn and improve.
Head of Engineering at The Kreativ Studio, leading a fully remote team across multiple product and client builds while staying close to the work.
Contributed across client builds, internal systems, training, and community programs at IGHub, bringing strong engineering execution and a clear understanding of the broader work around the product.
Led the Crunchies redesign across a 7-month engagement, improving delivery flows with Next.js, Tailwind CSS, and Google Maps integration.
Created and reviewed 50+ technical articles, built demos, and supported hackathon programs during a 3+ year run at Hackmamba.

experience.summary: I lead a remote engineering team across 10+ client and internal web products, steering architecture, sprint planning, and code reviews while staying active in the codebase myself.
highlights: My week centers on technical roadmaps and sprint planning for products in development, including Merphils (school operations and academic records) and Grooovy (event discovery, ticketing, and host tools).
Keeping our architectural standards sharp and our CI/CD pipelines tuned lets the team ship in under 15 minutes.

experience.summary: Working closely with founders from early requirements to launch, I’ve built and shipped 15+ custom web applications.
highlights: From database schema to checkout, I built Bonjour Quick Bites end to end in Next.js and TypeScript for outlet pickup and doorstep delivery.
On the education side, I built flashcards and quizzes for nursing students in Noma and authored the software engineering curriculum powering Alchemy Of Code.
For The Iroko Circle, I designed and developed a WordPress home for publishing African literature, accepting submissions, and connecting readers with local chapters.

experience.summary: Over two-plus years in Aba, I split my time between building client web apps, maintaining our internal tools, and teaching the next wave of local developers.
highlights: My engineering work ran across two parallel tracks: client-commissioned platforms and the internal tools that kept daily operations moving.
In the classroom, I trained and mentored 100+ web development students and wrote the foundational curriculum cohorts still learn from today.
Alongside the team, we hosted meetups and co-building sessions that brought together 300+ local tech builders.

experience.summary: Crunchies brought me on for a seven-month contract to lead the end-to-end redesign of Crunchies Online, helping grow monthly digital sales from ₦200k to over ₦3M.
highlights: Checkout, delivery zones, and pickup options were where orders used to stall, so I smoothed out those three friction points first.
To cut down on delivery address errors, I integrated the Google Maps API for real-time outlet lookup.
Rebuilding the frontend in Next.js and Tailwind CSS got load times under two seconds, even on slower mobile connections.

experience.summary: My long-form guides on React patterns, web performance, and developer tools appear on freeCodeCamp News, where tens of thousands of engineers have read them.
highlights: I break down tricky frontend topics through project-based walkthroughs and interactive code examples readers can try right away.
Several of my published guides consistently rank on Google page 1 for core React and JavaScript searches.

experience.summary: Developer-tooling teams around the world relied on the 50+ articles and interactive demo apps I wrote, edited, and built over three-plus years at Hackmamba.
highlights: My writing covered 50+ in-depth tutorials, SDK integration guides, and API docs for SaaS and devtools platforms.
Rather than stopping at prose, I built working demo repositories showing how those tools fit into real projects.
We also ran global hackathons, where I helped review and evaluate dozens of community project submissions.

experience.summary: At MOUAU, I helped introduce over 200 university students to software engineering through hands-on workshops and practical bootcamps.
highlights: We organized and ran practical web development bootcamps that took 200+ students from first lines of code to real projects.
Outside group sessions, I mentored aspiring developers one-on-one as they prepared for their first tech internships.
Together with fellow leads, I helped host campus-wide tech conferences, hackathons, and networking events.

experience.summary: On the engineering team at Truparse, I spent six months shipping React and TypeScript frontend features inside two-week agile sprints.
highlights: Day to day, we worked through agile sprint rituals, daily standups, and collaborative Git workflows to get features into production.
I built responsive, accessible UI components in React and TypeScript that held up across screen sizes.
When client WordPress sites needed a refresh, I wrote custom CSS to modernize their look and layout.

experience.summary: My first taste of production fintech came as a four-month intern, where I earned team recognition within two months for helping get features out faster.
highlights: My day-to-day work focused on modular HTML5, React.js, and CSS for customer-facing financial interfaces.
Pairing with senior engineers, I refactored legacy stylesheets into cleaner, reusable CSS components.
We also built and launched company marketing sites using WordPress, Bootstrap, and Sass.

projects.title: Crunchies Online
description: Crunchies Fried Chicken hired me to redesign its online ordering site over seven months. The redesign focused on checkout, especially how customers choose delivery or pickup and find the right outlet.

projects.title: Bonjour Quick Bites
description: An online storefront for ordering fresh bread, pastries, hot meals, and celebration cakes in Port Harcourt, with outlet pickup or doorstep delivery.
I built the platform end to end with Next.js and TypeScript, pairing Supabase for the database with Better Auth for authentication, while GitHub and Vercel handle version control and CI/CD.
For UI direction, I turned to Mobbin and leaned on its MCP server alongside the Vercel and GitHub MCP servers throughout development.

projects.title: The Iroko Circle
description: The Iroko Circle brings readers and writers together around African literature. Its website publishes new writing and gives visitors ways to submit work, join a chapter, and sign up for the newsletter.

projects.title: Noma
description: Noma helps nurses prepare for their exams with flashcards for reviewing key concepts and quizzes for testing what they know.

projects.title: Merphils
description: Merphils is a school management platform in development. The goal is to give staff tools for daily operations and let families and students access academic records without juggling separate accounts.

projects.title: Grooovy
description: Grooovy is an event platform in development for finding nights out you might otherwise hear about through friends or group chats. It brings public event listings, ticketing, and host tools together.

projects.title: Alchemy Of Code
description: Alchemy Of Code is a learning platform based on my curriculum. It helps learners master software engineering fundamentals and become well-rounded builders who can take an idea from concept to working software.
The platform runs on Cloudflare, with Supabase for its database and Better Auth for authentication.
